Replay

Device controls and signal actions

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Use Input_Binding(Control) to preserve button edges between Godot frames and simulation ticks. It interns InputMap names once and maps buffered button values to the game's Control type. Keep the binding outside World. A mapper can also read presentation-owned aim/device data through its borrowed user pointer. It must return a copied value without mutating the simulation.

Odin
bindings := [2]inputgd.Input_Action{{"ui_left", 0}, {"ui_right", 1}}
controls: inputgd.Input_Binding(Control)
ok := inputgd.input_binding_init(&controls, bindings[:], Control{},
    proc(_: rawptr, buttons: replay.Buttons) -> Control {
        return {move=i8(buttons.held & 2 != 0)-i8(buttons.held & 1 != 0)}
    })

// Once per engine frame; combine all applicable gates.
inputgd.input_binding_sample(&controls, {.Menu})
value := inputgd.input_binding_read(&controls)
// After a tick/control submission commits:
inputgd.input_binding_consume(&controls)

Up to 64 unique actions map to unique bits. Capture coalesces repeated presses of the same button within one simulation tick, while preserving simultaneous press and release. Reading does not consume; failed simulation steps keep their edges. Held state remains after consuming edges. For a Session, consume when session.control_consumed reports that a simulation step used the control. A successful frame call alone does not establish that. This helper does not change the runner's scheduling.

Paused, Unfocused, Menu and Inspecting gates return the supplied neutral Control and discard buffered edges. A button held across a gate transition must be released before reuse. Supply gates before sampling each frame; application code supplies focus/menu eligibility explicitly; the library does not infer it from an arbitrary Control node. Analog axes can be sampled in the mapper; applications with analog hold/rearm requirements must apply their own dead-zone policy. The engine-free replay.Control_Capture exposes the same bit/edge/gate behavior.

Signal actions#

Signal_Action(Action) connects a no-argument signal such as Button.pressed to a typed payload constructor and the existing Action_Intent. Keep it at a stable address. Emitter and user must outlive it; destroy/disconnect before freeing them.

Odin
buy: inputgd.Signal_Action(Action)
ok := inputgd.signal_action_init(&buy, button, "pressed",
    proc(user: rawptr) -> (Action, bool) {
        ui := cast(^Shop_UI)user
        return Action{item=ui.selected_item}, ui.selection_valid
    }, &shop_ui)

inputgd.signal_action_gate(&buy, gates) // cancel only unsubmitted input by default
sequence, error := inputgd.session_bound_action(&session, &buy)
for change in changes {
    inputgd.bound_action_observe(&buy, &session, change)
}

The payload is copied on the click. Another click while a payload awaits submission returns Capacity and preserves the first click. There is no hidden unbounded click queue. Call the submit helper every frame: backpressure/fencing retains the payload; accepted submission transfers delivery to the action ledger. room_bound_action provides the Room equivalent. Confirmed epoch-scoped results, including recovered tickets, remain in buy.intent; ordinary prediction cannot settle an action. Recovery reports are processed even while UI submission is gated.

Gates reject new captures. Default Cancel drops only unsubmitted work; Keep holds it until the gate clears. Neither can cancel work already accepted by the ledger. Update gate state before signals can arrive (including inside menu/focus handlers), then sample/submit in your frame loop. The library cannot infer when your UI became ineligible. Programmatic signal_action_capture uses the same typed latch. Signals with arguments should use a normal typed script handler to construct the action, or a separate adapter; this initial binding accepts no-argument signals.

Destroying a binding disconnects its callable and discards local tracking. It does not cancel an action already in a running Session. Consume results/recovery in order, and use explicit session lifecycle boundaries before reusing an owner. See intent contracts for counters and result semantics, and tests/replay_nodes/scripts/input.odin for the compile-checked engine example.
